content.text: {"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.8, "reasons": ["B puts backend-carrying instances in kernel vocabulary with `H.runner.local(...)` and `H.runner.ssh(...)`. That is a strike on dividing-line principle 7, which counts double. A keeps runners in `harness-dsl/runners`.", "B declares active states on kinds (`building`, `working`, `checking`, `reviewing`). It also models waiting on a human as a unit state, `roundsExhausted: ownerReview`. Principle 12 forbids both: a kind declares no active states, and waiting on a human is recorded once, on the attempt. A's kinds carry no active states, and A routes human waits through blocked attempts.", "B keeps two nouns for one pivot (`H.agent` alongside `H.seat`, against principle 22) and puts the per-harness share on the shared account (`.maxQuotaShare`). A folds agent into seat and moves the share to `pool.share(account, ratio)`. A's only bend is the principle 14 facets in `when`, which it declares and justifies."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.72, "reasons": ["Scenario 9 in A covers every requirement declaratively. The lane carries `.on(slaExtended, { update })`, and timers re-arm, so the old deadline never fires. Cost escalation is `.ceiling({ maxUsd: 0.4, onExceed: costCeiling })`. Pause and resume both record the metric value through `.resume(conversations, e => ...)`. B's 9 drops the Escalation lane, the cost ceiling and an explicit SLA extension. Its `conversations.resume()` takes no reason, so the resume is not recorded with the value that caused it.", "B's scheduling policies compare raw strings where A uses entities. Examples are `lane === heartbeats.name` and `choice.unit.kind === Feature.name ? Feature : Bug`. A uses entity-keyed `.priority(heartbeats, bugs, ...)`, `.wip`, `.boost` and `Dims { seat, model, facets }`.", "B's Tenancy suspend and churn are a workaround: a `status` field in the unit data, matched by update-stream `where` predicates. A expresses them as typed signals with lane reactions (`.on(suspend, { enter: Suspended })`). A's one blemish, the leftover `decomposeEpic` placeholder lane, is minor by comparison."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.74, "reasons": ["A connects lanes by identity everywhere. Its scheduler uses `candidate.lane === heartbeats`, and its seat policy reads `where: { kind: unit.kind, seat, model: sonnet }`. B compares by string in `candidate.lane === features.name` and `c.unit.lane === features.name`, so a name stands in for the pivot.", "B derives `bugLane = bugs.from(...)` from `bugs = H.lane('bugs').of(bug)`, which leaves two descriptors under one name. Its metrics and trigger then reference the bare `bugs` and `heartbeats`, while the harness registers `bugLane` and `heartbeatLane`: hidden coupling between the two descriptors. A builds each lane once and references that same entity in `H.entered(heartbeats, unhealthy)` and `H.create(bugs, ...)`.", "B's merge of facet into resource makes members runtime strings (`category.is(s.classify.category)`), and its design admits this loses entity identity. It also needs two lane-specific metrics, picked by lane name, to express one 'success by kind' dimension. A keeps `H.facet` and one `unitSuccess` metric keyed by kind and seat."]}

{"winner": "B", "confidence": 0.72, "reasons": ["Surface is 219 for B against 371 for A, with the same 12/12 coverage. B's `H` exposes one `H.on.*` source family, one `H.trigger(name, source, effect)` form and one `ctx` flow body. A carries `H.events.*` (nine streams), `H.time.*`, `H.call`, `Stream.streak/credit/where`, `Metric.crossing` and `Hysteresis`, plus a declarative flow algebra (`step/halt/when/loop/parallel/spawn/exit`).", "A's lane `handle(flow, { exits, retry })` requires an `exits` label map and a `retry` object even on trivial lanes. Scenario 04 writes `retry: { retries: 0, backoff: 'none', exhausted: down }` just to say \"no retry\". B's lanes in 04 are one line each, `H.lane('heartbeats', Heartbeat).handler(heartbeatFlow).suppliers(heartbeatClock)`, and rely on a kernel default.", "B has economy costs of its own. It keeps the deprecated `failsTo`, which it admits breaks principle 12, and it has granular `H.ops.*` booleans. It also declares active states per kind (`backup-running`, `incident-paging`) that principle 12 says are unnecessary. These are smaller than A's split of `Seat`, `Skill` and `Role`, its `Resource.is` / `ResourceValue` pair, and its `job.batch` + `job.every` + `job.detect` + `command.detect` options."]}

{"winner": "B", "confidence": 0.7, "reasons": ["B compares lanes by descriptor identity (`candidate.lane === heartbeats`), and its model policy reads metrics keyed by entities (`where: { kind: unit.kind, seat, model: sonnet }`). A couples through names instead: `c.unit.lane === features.name` picks the metric, and the scheduler ranks with `laneOrder.indexOf(candidate.lane)` over `.name` strings. That is hidden coupling through strings.", "A merges facet into resource, so one noun now covers both a lockable shared thing and a classification value. Its own notes admit that `category.is('billing').exclusive()` is legal. B keeps `H.facet` and `H.resource` as distinct entities, each with a clear pivot role.", "B's tracker store maps kernel states to tracker statuses by entity (`[todo, 'Todo']`), and its sources and consequences are named top-level pivots (`H.entered`, `H.create`). A keys the tracker map by state name (`[queued.name]: 'Todo'`) and loads the lane with source and consequence roles (`lane.create`, `lane.move`, `lane.cancel`)."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.78, "reasons": ["Surface 219 vs 371 with the same 12/12 coverage. B carries entities that A does without: `H.skill` beside `H.role`, `H.seat`, `H.journal` plus `.journals()`, `H.grant`, `H.events.*` streams, `H.metric` with `.by/.window/.crossing`, and `H.time.*`.", "Scenario 4 shows the gap in what each variant decides. A writes `H.on.streak(Heartbeat, 'heartbeat-down', 3, ...)` and `H.policy.scheduler` with `start`/`preempt`. B needs a hand-built `open-incidents` sum metric just to know whether an incident is open, and every command needs `.runner().effect().run(async ... ctx.exec ...)` ceremony.", "B duplicates mechanisms. Lane `exits` maps with `{to, atMost, then}` sit beside a separate `retry` block. Role carries `prompt` and `promptFile` while skill also carries `prompt`. `Resource.exclusive()` sits beside `ResourceValue.exclusive()`. A's equivalents are one `retry(policy, exhausted)` and a flow that returns states."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.62, "reasons": ["Scenario 6 in A states its rules in names a reader can predict. `.parallel('reviews', call => ({ a: call(reviewerA, ...), b: call(reviewerB, ...) }))` shows two seats on one role running side by side. `ctx.remember(factLessons, ...)` and `tasteJournal.record(...)` read directly. B runs the two critiques as sequential `.step`s and makes the reader learn `seat.call(skill)`.", "B's scenario 6 makes the reader write backend plumbing: a hand-written `http.store({ load, save })` with fetch calls and a `cmsRecord.harnessState` field, plus a raw `supply.poll({ fetch })`. A says the same thing declaratively with `rest.poll({ ... key, data })` and `rest.store({ ... schema })`. Under the Laravel framing, the framework should decide the shape and keep that plumbing away from the author.", "B's metric API needs more explaining. In `H.events.decisions(editorReview, { credit: d => d.actedOn.map(r => r === 'a' ? reviewerA : reviewerB) })` the credit function is opaque, and `metrics.read(x, { window, where: { seat, model: leading } })` takes a window at read time. A's `H.metric(...).rate(event => event.decision.actedOn.some(name => name === event.seat)).by('seat').window('30d')` builds the metric in one predictable chain."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.62, "reasons": ["A's builder chains read uniformly: `.handle(flow, map).exits({...})` and `seat.call(skill)` at each step. B's `.handle(review, { exits, retry, input })` packs three concerns into one options bag. B's staged drafts (`SeatDraft→SeatRole→SeatSkill`, `CommandDraft→CommandInput→CommandBody`) force a fixed call order that a reader must learn and that compile-errors when reordered, for example `.input(z.object({}))` on a no-input command.", "In scenario 6, B's `critiqueActedOn` rate relies on an invisible kernel rule. `event.seat` is populated from the seats whose outputs the context mapper 'fed', and nothing in the line says so. A's `H.events.decisions(editorReview, { credit: d => d.actedOn.map(...) })` states the credit explicitly where it is used.", "B scatters supplier and store vocabulary across `rest.poll`, `folder.files`, `schedule.cron` and `manual(name)`, each with a different options shape and a required `name`. Its metric reads are positional (`metrics.read(builderSuccess, builder, sonnet, kind)`), so the meaning of each argument depends on `.by` order. A's `metrics.read(m, { window, where: { seat, model } })` is self-describing."]}

{"winner": "B", "confidence": 0.64, "reasons": ["A puts backends into kernel vocabulary: `H.runner.local(...)` and `H.runner.ssh(name, { host, user, key, slots })` live on `H.*`. That breaks dividing-line principle 7, a double strike. B moves runners to the `harness-dsl/runners` subpath.", "A keeps `maxQuotaShare` on the account instance. The account is shared across harnesses, so a per-harness cap sits on a shared instance, which blurs principle 8's instance/pivot line. B puts the cap on the pool pivot with `pool.share(account, ratio)` and explains the move in its notes.", "B openly declares its one bend: facets added to the memory envelope's `when` (principle 14). Its remaining issues are raw-string comparisons, such as `e.to === inconclusive.name` and the string-keyed `trackerStates` record. These are lighter strikes than A's kernel-level backend leak."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.66, "reasons": ["In scenario 9, A keeps the category an entity end to end. `category.is(e.facet(category))` scopes both the Audit and the memory item, and per-key hysteresis on `approvalRate.crossing({ below: 0.9, above: 0.95, samples: 50 })` does the deduplication. B scopes the recorded experience with `when: { roles: [drafterRole], skills: [c] }`, so a raw string stands in for the category.", "B carries workarounds in its scenario files. Scenario 1 has a dead `decomposeEpic` that spawns into `H.lane('features-placeholder', Feature)` with `() => []`, then `void decomposeEpic`. Scenario 8 targets tenancies with `unit => unit.state === 'Customer'` as a string test.", "B's `during: { build: Building, audit: Auditing }` invents kind states for where an active attempt stands in its work, which principle 12 assigns to the attempt's current step. A expresses the same work through steps and the attempt status `blocked`/`suspended`, with no duplicate states."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.72, "reasons": ["B puts runner backends in the kernel namespace (`H.runner.local`, `H.runner.ssh`), which breaks principle 7, a dividing-line principle. A keeps them in `harness-dsl/runners`.", "B's kinds declare active states (`inProgress`, `probing`, `releasing`, `running`), and its startup check rejects 'a kind with two active states'. That contradicts principle 12, under which a kind declares no states for the active position and the attempt's current step is read from the ledger. A's kinds declare no active states.", "Durable execution: A's account shares live on the pool (`pool.share(account, 0.6)`), so one account descriptor serves both harnesses and principle 11's one-name rule holds unbent. B relaxes that rule to 'per harness' so it can keep `maxQuotaShare` on the account. A's own known bends (raw string members via `resource.is(v)`, decisions inside `when` dropped from flow state) are lesser strikes."]}

{"winner": "B", "confidence": 0.6, "reasons": ["Scenario 05: B ties the 09:00 cut-off to the flow through typed entities. `H.when.timer(loadLane, …)` sends the signal `approvalExpired`, and the lane declares `.on(approvalExpired, { at: ['approval'], enter: Expired })` against a typed step name. A uses `H.on.deadline(NightlyLoad, …, ['scheduled'])` with `act.move('expired')`, and must rely on the unit still being in its pending state `scheduled` while it actually waits on a halt. That is an implicit coupling between unit state and attempt position.", "B names its pivots explicitly. `seat.pool(apiPool)` and `journal.readBy(summarizerRole).recordedBy(approverRole)` state who serves and who reads and records. In A the pool serves seats implicitly, and the approver's taste writes link to no role, only to the `H.ops.writeMemory` grant. That is weaker connectedness.", "B's worst case is less bad than A's. It has a string `kind: 'Tenancy'` in `sqlite.scan` and an admitted gap where a loop round cannot read the previous round's deficits, but no hidden cross-kind coupling. A's worst case is a cost ceiling and deadline semantics spread across lane, kind and state, with journals unregistered on the harness."]}

{"winner": "B", "confidence": 0.77, "reasons": ["Scenario 8 Tenancy: A declares `suspended` and `churned` but nothing ever moves a unit into them. It has no supplier route, trigger or reaction for suspend, reinstate or churn. B routes billing events to `suspend`, `reinstate` and `churn` signals with `.on(suspend, { enter: Suspended })` and similar reactions, expressing 'suspended and reinstated any number of times'.", "Scenario 8 Negotiation: A detects the vendor walking away by starting a whole new attempt whose first step is `.when(s => s.input.vendorWalkedAway === true, f => f.exit('they-walked'))`, a workaround that spends an attempt (a round) on an outside event. B maps the replies to typed signals (`vendorCountered`, `vendorAccepted`, `vendorWalkedAway`) that update the unit or enter the terminal state directly.", "Scenario 8 Experiment: A hides the hourly metric collection inside a `job.collect` poll, so no recorded step exists per hour. B writes `loop('hourly', ... .step('measure').wait('nextHour'), { max: 336 })`, which states 'a command every hour for two weeks' honestly and holds no capacity while it waits."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.64, "reasons": ["Scenario 11 in B builds two descriptors that share one name. `counselReview = H.halt('counsel', ...)` is followed by `counsel = counselReview.policy(...)`. The skip policy filters on `counselReview.resolved()`, while the report and the grant use `counsel`. This is a hidden identity split that principle 11 forbids. A keeps one `counsel` halt, and its policy refers back to that same entity.", "A connects grouped metric triggers to the facet by identity with `H.on.metric(by: Facet<V>, ...)`. In B, `MetricSource` has only `groups?: G[]`, so the group key is not tied to the declared `H.facet`. B also keeps `job` beside `ctx.batch` as two words for submit-and-collect. A folds the job into `command.collect`.", "In B's scenario 11, finance rejection maps to `'declined'`, the same state as the second counsel return. Two different decisions land in one terminal state. A keeps `rejected`, `declined` and `stalled` distinct, each linked to its own cause (signoff halt, the `times: 2` trigger, the lane retry)."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.68, "reasons": ["Scenario 02's external cancellation is clearer in A. The webhook `read` returns `{ update: body.ticket, patch: { latest }, state: 'classifying' }` for 'customer-replied', which says directly where the unit goes. B's webhook carries only `schema: conversationSchema`, so how a reply cancels a blocked approval depends on the unstated 'signal arrives at a blocked-on-a-halt unit' rule in design.md. A durable-execution reader can follow A's line by line.", "A's flows are plain async code: `await ctx.halt(replyApproval, draft.value.reply, { category })` and a `for` loop over rounds. Resumption is replay by sequence number, so every line reads like a normal workflow. B's flow is a combinator chain (`.when(s => !s.steps.approval.approved, rejected => rejected.exit('rejected'))`) plus an exits map with `rejected: { to: fresh, maxTimes: 2, then: escalated }`. To predict what happens, the reader has to cross-reference the label in the flow with the lane.", "B's safe-category policy needs three separate `H.metric(...)` declarations, registered with `.metrics(...)`, plus a trigger `autoApproveSafe ... .do(H.ops.resolve(approval).by(safeCategory))` just to wire policy resolution. A puts it on the halt itself: `.policy(H.policy.rule('safe-category-skips-approval', safeCategory))`. A also reads sample counts inline via `rate.samples >= 200 && rate.hits === rate.samples`, so there are fewer things to explain."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.72, "reasons": ["In B's scenario 01, `decomposeEpic` spawns into `H.lane('features-placeholder', Feature)` with `() => []` and then needs `void decomposeEpic`. That is a dead workaround a newcomer would have to puzzle out. A's `ctx.spawn(features, plan.value.features)` followed by `ctx.wait('decomposed', { children })` expresses the Epic hierarchy directly.", "B's Bug and Feature kinds declare the active states `Building`, `Auditing` and `Planning` and map them through `during`. This re-models the attempt's current step as kind states, which principle 12 says a kind does not declare. A's kinds carry only `todo` and its terminals, so the lifecycle is stated without that misrepresentation.", "A's build-and-audit loop passes the auditor's deficits into the next round explicitly (`feedback = audit.value.deficits.join('\\n')`) and halts on `built.value.question` through `ctx.halt(ownerDecision, ...)`. B leaves the deficit handoff implicit ('fix every deficit the auditor left in the worktree'), so the loop's data flow is harder to express and to verify."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.62, "reasons": ["Re-entry in A is declared and predictable. In scenario 2, `rejected: { to: fresh, maxTimes: 2, then: escalated }` and `failed: { tries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', ... then: escalated }` say in the lane's exit map where a rejected draft goes and when re-entry stops. B hides that bound in a local `for (let round = 0; round < 3; round++)` loop inside an async `does` body. It replays by sequence number, so a durable reader must trust that the local state rebuilds deterministically.", "A gives every durable point a stable name: `.step('classify', ...)`, `.halt('approval', approval, ...)`, `.step('send', sendReply, ...)`, and resumption is keyed on that address plus the flow hash. The outside-cancellation rule (signal while blocked on a halt cancels as `interrupted` and re-queues) is a stated rule a reader can find. B's webhook returns `{ update, state: 'classifying' }` and leaves the reader to infer that this cancels the halted attempt.", "B reads more naturally line by line, for example `.maxUsdPerUnit(0.4)` and `halt.policy(rule)`. But its scenario 2 has a gap: the cost ceiling blocks on `H.halts.costCeiling`, which the reviewer's `H.ops.resolve(replyApproval, escalationHandled)` grant never names. In A, `.ceiling({ maxUsd: 0.4, onExceed: costCeiling })` and `H.ops.resolve(costCeiling)` sit visibly side by side."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.7, "reasons": ["B openly breaks principle 14 by adding facets to the memory envelope's `when` (\"14 (bent, knowingly)\"). Its scenario 06 then scopes taste with `facets: [section.is(...)]` instead of the resources principle 8 names for sections. A scopes section taste with `H.resource('sports')`/`opinion` and reports no principles broken.", "In 06, B's A/B metrics `actedOnA`/`actedOnB` key on decision fields 'a'/'b' rather than on the seat. A uses `H.events.credits(editorDecision, ...)` and reads `where: { seat }`, so a model swap keeps the series (principle 8). B's policy is also two derived closures in place of one seat-keyed policy.", "B's lane carries `pause(reason: string)`, and its scenario 01 orders lanes by `lane.name` strings (`laneOrder: readonly string[]`). A compares lanes by descriptor identity (`candidate.lane === heartbeats`) and records the pause cause from the crossing. That makes A more faithful to 'a string never stands in' for an entity."]}

{"winner": "B", "confidence": 0.62, "reasons": ["Principle 8 names the memory pivot 'journal = memory kind × store × recall'. B uses that noun (`H.journal`, `Journal`). A keeps `H.library`, a word the principles never use, which strains principles 8, 9 and 22 on a dividing-line principle.", "On scenario 8, B marks `a-wins` and `b-wins` as `'neutral'`, matching 'none of these is failure' without claiming a success. A sets `aWins` and `bWins` to `'success'`, which puts experiments into the success rate as a judgement the owner did not make."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.66, "reasons": ["Scenario 4, the focus, has a lie in B: Incident's failure exits go to `needsEngineering`, a waiting state, so the kind has no failure terminal. B's `stillBroken: { to: queued, maxTimes: 3 }` reruns the whole runbook, including `pageOnCall`, which is marked `effect('repeatable')` even though paging is wrong to repeat. A's incident flow ends in a `Resolved`/`Unresolved` pair of terminals and declares the runbook `afterCrash: 'park'`.", "Durability: A's `loop` resumes 'at the first unrecorded iteration' and `wait('nextHour')` holds no capacity, so Experiment is a single attempt over two weeks. B emulates the hourly ticks by re-offering `known` units through a schedule `updatesOnly()`. That is a workaround that turns one experiment into roughly 336 attempts, and it uses the flow's `startedAt` from `u.createdAt` to decide termination.", "In Scenario 4, B's disk preflight is a flow step that B must repeat in both the backup and renewal flows. A expresses it as `Runner.preflight(diskSpacePreflight)` on the host, alongside `.slots(1)`. A also uses typed `H.when.pattern(..., consecutive: 3, per: service)` and `admit(backups, count(incidents,'active','waiting')===0)`, which state the preemption rule directly. B's equivalent is a hand-sorted schedule policy built on `load()` arithmetic."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.7, "reasons": ["A connects scheduling to lanes by entity identity (`candidate.lane === heartbeats`, `marking.count(incidents, 'active', 'waiting')`). B's scenario 1 couples through names instead (`candidate.lane === features.name`, `c.unit.lane === features.name`), and its `ScheduleChoice.paused: readonly string[]` and `lane.pause(reason: string)` are raw strings standing in for entities.", "In scenario 10, B needs a hoisted `function smokeLane() { return smokes; }` to let the release flow reference the smoke lane. That is a hidden declaration-order coupling. A's `.spawn('smoke', smoke, ...)` references the lane directly, with no indirection.", "A keeps each concept on one noun with clear pivots: `seat.batch(skill)` makes batch a step of the seat, `H.events.credits(halt, ...)` keys on seats, and facet stays distinct from resource. B's facet-into-resource merge lets `category.is(...)` be leasable, which blurs what a resource connects to, as its own design notes admit."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.65, "reasons": ["A's flows read as plain async code a newcomer predicts line by line: `await ctx.halt(replyApproval, draft.value.reply, { category: kindOfIssue })`, then `ctx.run(sendReply, ...)`. B's typed step-chain needs explaining. Its `.halt(...)` takes `when`, `skip` and `facets` options, the step output can be `D | undefined`, and its design concedes 'a loop round cannot read the previous round's output'. In scenario 1 the builder never sees the auditor's deficits in code.", "B spreads one scenario's meaning across more concepts a reader must learn. Scenario 2 introduces signals plus reactions (`.on(customerReplied, { update, enter: New })`), routers (`to.signal`, `to.skip`), a separately registered `H.metric(...).samples(...)` that digs `event.seats.find(a => a.seat.name === drafter.name)`, and `.metrics(approvalRate)` on the harness. A expresses approval rate by model directly with `rateBy({ ..., by: { modelOf: choice.seat } })` and by category with `by: category`.", "Laravel lens: A decides more consistently with a smaller surface (222 vs 350). One `H.state(name, position, verdict?)` builder, and `lane.retries(n, { exhausted })` read uniformly across lanes. B splits state declaration into `H.state` and `H.terminal`, requires a `.retry` on every lane even where no retry is meant (`maxAttempts: 1`), and requires `H.cancel` reactions on lanes, all ceremony a reader must learn."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.77, "reasons": ["B declares active states on kinds (`H.state('loading').active()`, `building`, `running`), which breaks principle 12 as ruled: 'a kind declares no states for it'. A deletes `during` and active states, so the step is the active position.", "B puts a backend into kernel vocabulary with `H.runner.ssh(...)` and `H.runner.local(...)`, a dividing-line strike on principle 7. A keeps runners in subpaths (`ssh.host`, `local.runner`).", "B keeps two nouns for one pivot (`H.agent` and `H.seat`, both of entity sort 'seat'), against principle 22. A has one `H.seat` whose fixed-model form is the principle-8 agent."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.72, "reasons": ["A deletes `H.agent` (B keeps both `H.agent(name).role(r).model(m)` and `H.seat`, typed as the same `EntityRef<'seat'>`). That is two builders for one pivot, and every B scenario mixes them.", "A folds retry into the required `failed` exit and drops `lane.unitOf`. B's lane carries a separate `.retry({..., exhausted})` plus `unitOf(candidate)`, and B's scenario 9 needs `unitOf` for time-to-breach scoring, where A uses `candidate.unit.deadline`. A's lane has fewer methods for the same coverage.", "Durable lens: A's `pause()`/`resume()` take a `Crossed` payload, so the recorded pause carries the metric that caused it without a free-text reason. B's `pause(reason: string)` returns `Consequence<unknown>`, which is a raw string and a looser surface. A's few additions (`known`, `memory.read`, `manual<D>`) each serve a named scenario and are not one-use extras."]}

{"winner": "A", "confidence": 0.8, "reasons": ["A connects flow outcomes to kind states through a lane pivot: a flow ends in `.exit('parked')` and `topics.exits({ parked, delivered, failed: {... then: unfinished} })` maps labels to state entities. B's flows return raw state strings (`return 'parked'`, `ctx.wait('awaiting-features', ...)`), and its lanes name exhaustion by string (`.retry(threeAttempts, 'abandoned')`), so the flow is coupled to the kind's state names.", "A makes the grant a named pivot that references the halt by identity: `H.grant(supervisor, H.ops.resolve(ownerDecision), ...)`. B folds grants into a vendor adapter, `claude.supervisor({ grants: [...] })`, and scenario 1 uses the capability-style `H.ops.resolveHalts`, which names no halt (principle 17).", "A addresses metrics by entity: `H.events.executions(checkCitations)` reads the citation pass rate per seat and model through the seat pivot. B builds the same metric as an ad-hoc filter object, `{ entry: 'invocation' as const, executable: citationCheck, status: 'ended' }`, and indexes the result by name (`byModel[opus.name]`), so the model is looked up by string."]}

{"winner": "B", "confidence": 0.7, "reasons": ["A declares itself in breach: its design notes say principle 14 is 'bent, knowingly' because the memory envelope's `when` gains `facets`. In scenario 6 the section scope is then a string facet (`section.is(event.context.section)`), where principle 8 names a section as a resource that 'a string never stands in for'. B declares sections as entities (`H.resource('sports')`, `H.resource('opinion')`) and scopes taste with `resources: sectionScope(...)`.", "Principle 8 says metrics on an A/B comparison key on the seat. B does this directly: `H.events.credits(editorDecision, ... => reviewerA : reviewerB)` and `metrics.read(critiqueActedOn, { where: { seat } })`. A keys its two rates on `actedOn === 'a' | 'b'` literals in the decision payload, so the series is tied to string labels rather than to the seat entity.", "B lists 'Principles broken: none' and its scenario 6 holds to that. B removed `pause(reason: string)` and kept metric columns to the seven in principle 18.
